tier_reason: docs/BENCHMARKS.md (generated by tools/pixel-compare/src/main.rs bench-compare against tools/cpp-renderer/src/main.cpp run_bench) states compilers and CPU, and flags are recoverable from Cargo.toml and tools/cpp-renderer/CMakeLists.txt, which would formally meet A; but the two timed regions do different work in 5 of 11 demos (the C++ image_* demos re-read spheres.bmp from disk and the flash_* demos re-open and parse shapes.txt inside every timed call, while Rust decodes an embedded BMP and caches the parsed shapes in a OnceLock), so this first-party comparison stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Best-of render time Rust/C++ on docs/BENCHMARKS.md (2026-07-22): simple_line 0.66x (0.22 vs 0.34 ms), image_transforms 0.73x, flash_rasterizer2 0.76x, flash_rasterizer 0.79x, lion_outline 0.86x, image_filters 0.87x, perspective 0.96x, image_perspective 0.98x, compositing2 0.99x, conv_dash_marker 1.02x, rasterizers2 1.08x; medians 0.56x (simple_line) to 1.26x (rasterizers2). Geometric mean of the best-of ratios is 0.87x over all 11 demos (about 1.15x faster, derived from page data), 0.91x over the 6 demos whose timed work is the same on both sides, and 0.98x (parity) over those 6 without the sub-millisecond simple_line (derived from page data). The largest wins (image_transforms, image_filters, flash_rasterizer, flash_rasterizer2) are confounded by C++-only file I/O and parsing inside the timed call; every absolute difference in the table is under 0.62 ms, below the project's own note that differences under about 2 ms are at the measurement floor.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.91.0, cargo build --release with [profile.release] lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1 (default opt-level 3) per Cargo.toml; MSVC 19.44.35219.0 x64 via CMake --config Release: tools/cpp-renderer/CMakeLists.txt sets no optimisation flags of its own (only /EHsc and warning suppressions), so CMake's default MSVC Release flags apply, and no whole-program optimisation (/GL, /LTCG) is enabled on the C++ side while Rust uses fat LTO. No target-cpu or -march flags on either side.
corrections.workload: Render-call time of 11 AGG 2.6 demo scenes (simple_line 512x512, lion_outline 512x512, rasterizers2 500x450, conv_dash_marker 500x330, perspective 600x600, image_perspective 600x600, image_transforms 430x340, image_filters 430x340, compositing2 600x400, flash_rasterizer 655x520, flash_rasterizer2 655x520), output pinned byte-identical to the C++ reference by committed tests; 4 passes x 25 timed iterations after 2 warmups per pass, best and median over pooled samples. Rust timed in-process (pixel-compare); C++ timed inside the agg-render bench subprocess with std::chrono::steady_clock around each demo function call.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 12 stars, 2 forks; crates.io agg-rust 1.1.0 with 1,660 downloads
corrections.caveats: Rust port of AGG 2.6 (ghaerr/agg-2.6 is already a wave 10 rasterizers-2d record), so a likely duplicate under the ports rule; the numbers are its own Rust-versus-AGG-C++ harness, not AGG's vello_chart numbers. Language is Rust, outside the C++ filter, and Cargo.toml declares no C ABI library target. The baseline is AGG itself, not Skia, Cairo or Blend2D. Harness asymmetry: the C++ image_transforms, image_filters and image_perspective functions call headless::load_spheres() (fopen/fread of spheres.bmp plus a repack copy) inside the timed call, and flash_rasterizer/flash_rasterizer2 open and parse shapes.txt from disk on every call, while the Rust side decodes an include_bytes! BMP and caches the parsed shapes in a OnceLock (commit 'Cache flash shapes parse to reach C++ parity in flash demos'); the docs claim that no asset loading or file I/O is timed is therefore not true for the C++ side. On the 6 symmetric demos Rust is at parity (geomean 0.91x, 0.98x without the 0.34 ms simple_line). Rust is built with fat LTO and one codegen unit while the C++ side has no LTCG. Old 2-core laptop CPU (i7-7660U) on Windows 10, single run date, and the project itself says differences under about 2 ms are at the measurement floor; all measured differences are under 0.62 ms.

notes: Numbers on docs/BENCHMARKS.md and README match the record exactly; metadata (BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2026-07-22, 12 stars, not a fork) checks out. Treat as a port of the wave 10 AGG record (ghaerr/agg-2.6) and likely fold it as a duplicate; if kept, its evidence shows parity with AGG rather than a clear win, and the apparent wins come from C++-side file I/O and parsing in the timed region. Language field is already Rust (mismatch with the C++ filter).
